records.label: spacr.qt.resonance.set_now_playing#1
records.source: THE ANALYSIS IS READ HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE, which is the whole reason this is a setter rather than a variable. :func:`playing_moment` is called once a frame from the backdrop's clock, which runs on the GUI thread; a ``stat`` there is a filesystem call on the GUI thread, and on a network home directory that is exactly the stall spaCR has :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe` for. This runs on the audio thread, which has just rendered the file and is the right place to open it.
records.context: The analysis is read here and nowhere else, which is the whole reason this is a setter rather than a variable. :func:`playing_moment` is called once a frame from the backdrop's clock, which executes on the main GUI execution path; a ``stat`` there is a filesystem call on the main GUI execution path, and on a network home directory that is exactly the stall spaCR has :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe` for. This executes on the audio independent execution path, which has just rendered the file and is the right place to open it.
records.translation: GREININGIN ER LESIN HÉR OG HVERGI ANNARS STAÐAR, sem er öll ástæðan fyrir því að þetta er stillifall frekar en breyta. :func:`playing_moment` er kallað einu sinni á hvern ramma frá klukku bakgrunnsins, sem keyrir á GUI-þræðinum; ``stat`` þar er skráakerfiskall á GUI-þræðinum, og á heimamöppu á neti er það einmitt stöðvunin sem spaCR hefur :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe` fyrir. Þetta keyrir á hljóðþræðinum, sem hefur rétt í þessu teiknað skrána og er rétti staðurinn til að opna hana.

records.label: spacr.qt.resonance.settle#1
records.source: Each round is one Newton step onto the linearised zero set -- ``p -= t * w * grad(w) / |grad(w)|^2`` -- which lands on the nodal line in one step where the field is locally straight and converges in a handful where it is not. That is what the sand does, and it is cheaper than the gradient descent it replaces, which needs a step size that depends on the mode numbers.
records.context: Each round is one Newton step onto the linearised zero set -- ``p -= t * w * grad(w) / |grad(w)|^2`` -- which lands on the nodal line in one step where the field is locally straight and converges in a handful where it is not. That is what the sand does, and it is cheaper than the gradient descent it replaces, which needs a step size that depends on the mode numbers.
records.translation: Hver umferð er eitt Newton-skref á línulegaða núllmengið -- ``p -= t * w * grad(w) / |grad(w)|^2`` -- sem lendir á hnútalínunni í einu skrefi þar sem sviðið er staðbundið beint og samleitnar á fáeinum þar sem það er það ekki. Það er það sem sandurinn gerir, og það er ódýrara en stigulsniðurgangan sem það kemur í staðinn fyrir, sem þarf skrefstærð sem er háð háttatölunum.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.resonance.settle#2
records.source: ``tightness`` below 1 leaves the particles short of the lines, which is what a plate driven gently looks like: the sand gathers but does not resolve. It is the control that makes silence read as a loose cloud and a loud passage as a figure. It may be one number for every particle or ONE PER PARTICLE, and per particle is what the backdrop uses: a plate where every grain converges equally draws a wire diagram, and a real one has a haze of sand that never quite arrives. The haze is what makes the picture look like sand rather than like a plot of an equation.
records.context: ``tightness`` below 1 leaves the particles short of the lines, which is what a plate driven gently looks like: the sand gathers but does not resolve. It is the control that makes silence read as a loose cloud and a loud passage as a figure. It may be one number for every particle or one per particle, and per particle is what the backdrop uses: a plate where every grain converges equally draws a wire diagram, and a real one has a haze of sand that never quite arrives. The haze is what makes the picture look like sand rather than like a plot of an equation.
records.translation: ``tightness`` undir 1 skilur agnirnar eftir áður en þær ná línunum, sem er hvernig plata lítur út þegar hún er knúin varlega: sandurinn safnast en skerpist ekki. Það er stýringin sem lætur þögn lesast sem laust ský og háværan kafla sem mynstur. Það má vera ein tala fyrir allar agnir eða EITT FYRIR HVERJA ÖGN, og fyrir hverja ögn er það sem bakgrunnurinn notar: plata þar sem hvert korn samleitnar jafnt teiknar vírmynd, og raunveruleg plata hefur þoku af sandi sem kemst aldrei alveg alla leið. Þokan er það sem lætur myndina líta út eins og sand frekar en graf af jöfnu.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.annotate#10
records.source: A SUGGESTION IS JUDGED, NOT RELABELLED (item 512). A crop Suggest proposed a class for wears an amber ``?`` badge beside its dashed ring. A click or ``Y`` confirms it (it becomes an ordinary label and wears a green tick); a right-click or ``N`` rejects it (it goes back to unanswered and wears a red cross); ``U`` undoes either. The bar above the key legend says so, and counts what the page and the column hold. Each judgement is written to the ``<column>_verdict`` column as ``+c`` or ``-c``, so it survives a restart, and the next Suggest round is handed the rejections to train on. See :meth:`AnnotateScreen._judge` and :func:`spacr.suggest.verdict_column`.
records.context: A suggestion is judged, not relabelled (item 512). An extracted image region Suggest proposed a class for wears an amber ``?`` badge beside its dashed ring. A click or ``Y`` confirms it (it becomes an ordinary label and wears a green tick); a right-click or ``N`` rejects it (it goes back to unanswered and wears a red cross); ``U`` undoes either. The bar above the structured-data name legend says so, and counts what the page and the column hold. Each judgement is written to the ``<column>_verdict`` column as ``+c`` or ``-c``, so it survives a restart, and the next Suggest round is handed the rejections to train on. See :meth:`AnnotateScreen._judge` and :func:`spacr.suggest.verdict_column`.
records.translation: TILLAGA ER METIN, EKKI ENDURMERKT (liður 512). Myndskurður sem Suggest lagði til flokk fyrir ber rafgult ``?`` merki við hlið brotna hringsins. Smellur eða ``Y`` staðfestir hana (hún verður venjulegt merki og ber grænt hak); hægrismellur eða ``N`` hafnar henni (hún fer aftur í ósvarað og ber rauðan kross); ``U`` afturkallar hvort tveggja. Stikan fyrir ofan lyklaskýringuna segir þetta, og telur það sem síðan og dálkurinn geyma. Hvert mat er skrifað í ``<column>_verdict`` dálkinn sem ``+c`` eða ``-c``, svo það lifir af endurræsingu, og næsta Suggest-umferð fær hafnanirnar til að þjálfa á. Sjá :meth:`AnnotateScreen._judge` og :func:`spacr.suggest.verdict_column`.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.annotate#9
records.source: A PAGE IS WHAT FITS (item 512). The grid holds exactly the crops that fit the room the crop pane gives it, at the crop size the settings ask for, and it never scrolls: opening the console, folding a pane, changing the GUI scale or resizing the window recomputes the page and pushes the rest to the next one, the page counter follows, and the first crop on screen stays where it was. See :func:`grid_that_fits` and :meth:`AnnotateScreen._refit_grid`.
records.context: A page is what fits (item 512). The grid holds exactly the extracted image regions that fit the room the extracted image region pane gives it, at the extracted image region size the settings ask for, and it never scrolls: opening the console, folding a pane, changing the GUI scale or resizing the window recomputes the page and pushes the rest to the next one, the page counter follows, and the first extracted image region on application view stays where it was. See :func:`grid_that_fits` and :meth:`AnnotateScreen._refit_grid`.
records.translation: SÍÐA ER ÞAÐ SEM KEMST FYRIR (liður 512). Hnitanetið geymir nákvæmlega þá myndskurði sem komast fyrir í rýminu sem myndskurðarrúðan gefur því, í myndskurðarstærðinni sem stillingarnar biðja um, og það flettist aldrei: að opna skipanagluggann, brjóta saman rúðu, breyta GUI-kvarðanum eða breyta stærð gluggans endurreiknar síðuna og ýtir restinni á þá næstu, síðuteljarinn fylgir, og fyrsti myndskurðurinn á skjánum helst þar sem hann var. Sjá :func:`grid_that_fits` og :meth:`AnnotateScreen._refit_grid`.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.annotate.badge_colors#1
records.source: Item 512. A suggestion is amber, a confirmed suggestion green and a rejected one red -- the theme's own warning, success and error colours, so the badge follows a theme change the way the rest of the chrome does. The glyph is drawn in the theme's background colour, which is black on the dark theme and near-white on the light one; each of those fills was chosen against it and reads at better than 4.5:1 in both. None of the three is a class colour, so a badge is never read as a class.

records.source: A confirmation of class c stands while the crop is labelled c; a rejection of class c stands until the crop is labelled c after all. Relabelling a confirmed crop, or labelling a rejected one as the class that was rejected, withdraws the judgement, so the verdict column never says something the annotation column contradicts.
records.context: A confirmation of class c stands while the extracted image region is labelled c; a rejection of class c stands until the extracted image region is labelled c after all. Relabelling a confirmed extracted image region, or labelling a rejected one as the class that was rejected, withdraws the judgement, so the verdict column never says something the annotation column contradicts.
records.translation: Staðfesting á flokki c stendur á meðan myndskurðurinn er merktur c; höfnun á flokki c stendur þar til myndskurðurinn er þrátt fyrir allt merktur c. Endurmerking staðfests myndskurðar, eða merking hafnaðs myndskurðar sem flokkinn sem var hafnað, afturkallar matið, svo matsdálkurinn segir aldrei eitthvað sem athugasemdadálkurinn stangast á við.
